newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Tamil rebel chief seeks Blair's support.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Tamil rebel chief seeks Blair's support.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebel leader Velupillai Prabhakaran has written to new British Prime Minister Tony Blair seeking his government's support for the Tamil seperatist struggle.

"The Tamil Nation in Sri Lanka, which has been engaged in a long and determined struggle to freely choose its political status, looks upon your new government for support and sympathy to win its legitimate political rights," Prabhakaran told Blair.

A copy of the letter to Blair, whose Labour Party won Britain's general election last week, was faxed to Reuters from the International Secretariat of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils in the north and east of the the mainly Sinhalese island, which was a British colony until independence in 1947.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
